item.title: Alphabet, Numbers 1–20, Gender, and Articles
item.description: Lesson 2: Alphabet, Numbers 1–20, Gender, and Articles French nouns have gender: every noun is masculine or feminine, and that gender affects articles, adjectives, and pronouns. Gender in French is grammatical, not a statement about the thing itself, and it must be learned with each noun. This…

item.title: Être, Avoir, and Simple Sentences
item.description: Lesson 3: Être, Avoir, and Simple Sentences Être, to be, and avoir, to have, are the two most important verbs in French, and they are irregular, so they must be learned by heart. They appear in introductions, descriptions, age, feelings, and later in compound tenses, so learning them now saves time…

item.title: Regular Verbs, Present Tense, and Daily Routine
item.description: Lesson 4: Regular Verbs, Present Tense, and Daily Routine Most French verbs fall into regular groups, and learning the pattern for one verb lets you use many others. This lesson teaches the largest group, verbs ending in -er, plus a first set of -ir and -re verbs, and it uses them for daily…

item.title: Numbers to 100, Time, Days, and Places
item.description: Lesson 5: Numbers to 100, Time, Days, and Places Larger numbers, time, and days in French are regular with a few famous exceptions, and learning them now makes shopping, travel, and appointments possible. This lesson teaches numbers to 100, clock time, days and months, and place words with à, en…

item.title: Passé Composé, Adjectives, and Describing Things
item.description: Lesson 6: Passé Composé, Adjectives, and Describing Things The passé composé is the main past tense for spoken French, and it lets you talk about what you did yesterday, last week, and earlier. It is formed with an auxiliary verb, être or avoir, plus a past participle. Most verbs use avoir, and a…

item.title: Wanting, Liking, Ability, and Polite Requests
item.description: Lesson 7: Wanting, Liking, Ability, and Polite Requests Preference and requests in French use vouloir, to want, pouvoir, to be able to or may, aimer, to like, and polite forms with s'il vous plaît and je voudrais, I would like. These verbs are irregular, so their present forms must be learned, and…
